question: A financial services customer's legal stakeholder is reviewing a contract addendum before approving production rollout of a support agent that would use the code execution tool alongside web search. Legal asks whether all data associated with these two tools qualifies for the customer's required Zero Data Retention (ZDR) arrangement. What should the technical lead say?
options: A) Neither web search nor code execution can qualify for ZDR under any configuration, because ZDR applies only to the core model API and not to ancillary tools like web search or code execution; therefore legal should reject any support agent design that depends on these tools for this customer.

B) Both web search and code execution are always fully ZDR eligible because retention posture is determined solely by the model in use, not by which server-side tools are active; so long as the model itself is under a ZDR agreement, legal can approve the agent without tool-specific carve-outs.

C) Web search is ZDR eligible except when dynamic filtering is enabled while code execution is not ZDR eligible, so legal should not treat the combined workflow as meeting a blanket ZDR requirement unless dynamic filtering is off and code execution is handled separately.

D) ZDR eligibility is scoped solely to the Message Batches API and does not extend to real-time tool calls like web search or code execution, meaning the support agent's data flows are outside the ZDR agreement and legal should proceed without additional restrictions on these tools.
correct_answers: C) Web search is ZDR eligible except when dynamic filtering is enabled while code execution is not ZDR eligible, so legal should not treat the combined workflow as meeting a blanket ZDR requirement unless dynamic filtering is off and code execution is handled separately.
explanations: Incorrect. Web search can be ZDR eligible with dynamic filtering off, so a blanket rejection of both tools overstates the restriction.
Incorrect. ZDR eligibility depends on both the model and tools; code execution is documented as not ZDR eligible regardless of model, so tool-specific carve-outs are necessary.

Correct. Web search is ZDR eligible except when dynamic filtering is enabled, while code execution is not ZDR eligible, so a combined agent workflow requires careful treatment rather than blanket approval.
Incorrect. ZDR eligibility applies to features and models generally, not limited to Message Batches API; web search and code execution have their own ZDR statuses.
